findings.title: NPE when the 'Clients' all-resource is missing
findings.body:
When no per-client resource exists, `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` falls back to `getResourceTypeResource(...)`. That call returns null in two cases: `supportsAuthorizationSchema` is false (for example, realm admin permissions were disabled but the admin-permissions client still exists), or the 'Clients' resource was never created (realms initialized before this change, since `init()` returns early when the client exists).

The null is then passed directly to `getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)` and later to `resource.getScopes()`, which throws a NullPointerException. Every client admin endpoint called by an admin without manage-clients would return 500.

The sibling `hasPermission(String)` null-checks the resource; this branch should do the same and return false.

findings.title: Per-client deny on VIEW is bypassed by the all-clients VIEW check
findings.body:
`canView(ClientModel)` first calls `canView()`. That evaluates only the all-clients 'Clients' resource and returns true as soon as an all-clients VIEW permission grants. The client-specific resource is never consulted.

As a result, a negative per-client VIEW permission (all clients viewable except X) has no effect. `requireView(X)` succeeds, and `ClientsResource.getClients` (which computes `canView()` once) lists every client.

The user resource type tests (`testViewUserPermission`, `testImpersonatePermission`) establish that a resource-specific permission overrides the all-resource one, so client semantics are inconsistent. This is also untested.

findings.title: Any per-client permission suppresses all-clients grants for every other scope
findings.body:
If a resource exists for the client, only that resource is evaluated. Per-client resources are created without a type, and all-clients permissions are attached to the 'Clients' resource, so the policy evaluator never picks up the all-clients permissions for that client.

Example: an admin has an all-clients MANAGE permission and a per-client permission granting only MAP_ROLES on client X. `canManage(X)` then returns false, even though the admin can manage every other client.

The fallback should be per scope: when the specific resource yields no decision for the requested scope, also evaluate the all-clients resource. Otherwise only deny on the same scope should override.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the string 'Clients' instead of client ids
findings.body:
`resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` only matches resources whose type is 'Clients'. In the V2 schema that is just the all-clients resource created by `init()`; per-client resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` without a type.

The method therefore never returns real client ids. When an all-clients permission grants the scope, it returns `{"Clients"}` (the resource name), which callers will treat as a client id. Per-client grants are ignored entirely.

It should iterate per-client resources (or the policies attached to them) and return the client ids those resource names represent.

findings.title: canExchangeTo now throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token exchange under V2
findings.body:
Before this PR, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returned the V1 `ClientPermissions`. It now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `canExchangeTo` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

The token exchange provider calls `AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)` when exchanging to another client. With the V2 feature enabled, such requests will fail with a 500 instead of an access-denied response.

The unused `getEvaluationContext` helper and `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` import suggest this was meant to be implemented. At minimum it should return false or delegate rather than throw.

Similarly, `isPermissionsEnabled`/`setPermissionsEnabled` now throw. Those are reached from the `/clients/{id}/management/permissions` endpoints, which will return 500.

findings.title: canView() ignores all-clients MANAGE, inconsistent with canView(ClientScopeModel)
Repeated full policy evaluations per client in listings
findings.body:
Each `hasPermission` call evaluates the resource with all of its scopes and then checks a single scope. In the fallback path it also loads all policies of the 'Clients' resource just to test emptiness.

`canView(c)` alone triggers up to 4 evaluations: `canView()`, MANAGE via `canConfigure`, CONFIGURE, and VIEW. `getAccess(c)` repeats `canView`, `canManage` and `canConfigure`. Listing N clients therefore performs roughly 10+ evaluations and extra policy queries per client.

The granted scopes from one evaluation could be computed once per client (and the all-clients result once per request) and reused.

findings.title: getResourceName has no CLIENTS branch, so client permission resources render with null names
findings.body:
`getResourceName` maps USERS resources to "All users" or the username. For the new CLIENTS type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Neither per-client resources (created via `resourceStore.create(...)`) nor the 'Clients' all-resource (created in `init()`) have a display name, so this returns null.

Permission resource listings for client permissions will show empty names instead of "All clients" or the client's clientId.

findings.title: Realms already initialized never receive the new Clients resource and scopes
findings.body:
`init()` returns early when the admin-permissions client already exists. Realms that enabled admin permissions before this change never get:
- the 'Clients' all-resource;
- the new `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` and `map-roles-composite` scopes.

For those realms, creating a client permission fails ("Scope [configure] does not exist" / "No scopes found."). Evaluation also hits the null all-clients resource path in `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission`.

The schema should be reconciled for existing clients, adding missing scopes and resource-type resources.

findings.title: Javadoc for void require* methods says 'Returns true'
findings.body:
The new Javadoc on `requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", and `requireViewClientScopes()` has the same wording. Both methods are void and throw ForbiddenException on failure.

The docs should match the other require* methods: "Throws ForbiddenException if canView()/canViewClientScopes() returns false".

findings.title: Client removal no longer cleans up permission data; V2 has no replacement
findings.body:
The removal listener now runs only when V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. Previously it always cleaned up V1 client/role/group permission objects. If V1 permissions were created and the feature later disabled, deleting clients, roles or groups now leaves orphaned resources and policies.

Under V2, nothing removes the per-client resource and permissions created by `getOrCreateResource` when a client is deleted. Stale permissions referencing non-existent clients accumulate in the admin-permissions resource server.

findings.title: Test rotates the secret of the client used by the injected admin client and leaves other mutations unrestored
findings.body:
`testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `generateNewSecret()` and `invalidateRotatedSecret()` on `myclient`. That is the confidential client (secret "mysecret") the `realmAdminClient` authenticates with, and nothing restores the secret. Any later re-authentication or token refresh by `realmAdminClient` in this class will fail with 401, making results order-dependent.

Other tests have the same problem with no cleanup registered:
- `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and moves a default client scope to optional;
- `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles and maps one to `myadmin`.

These changes should be registered via `realm.cleanup()` or done on a dedicated client.
